successors.note: Murong Hui 'relocated the remnants of the commandery to the west within Liaodong' (Four Commanderies page); Goguryeo ruled Lelang directly only after 357 (K.H.J. Gardiner, same page).

Hwanghae passes to daifang-commandery; Zhenfan's placeholder (Gyeonggi) is assumed to go with the southern half, which no page states, so it is left out here.

region.text: Lelang, set up 'in Old Chosŏn after defeating the Wiman dynasty in 108 BCE'; capital Joseon prefecture at modern Pyongyang

ledger.note: 108 BCE: Han forces found Lelang Commandery on the ruins of Wiman Joseon at Pyongyang. 'established in Old Chosŏn after defeating the Wiman dynasty in 108 BCE'; the Four Commanderies page has 'three commanderies were established in its place: Lelang, Lintun, and Zhenfan'. Year and place are the pages'; the outline is the researcher's reading.

region.text: Zhenfan Commandery, 'absorbed into Lelang in 82 BCE'; location unclear on the page, placed south of Lelang by Bowman

ledger.note: 82 BCE: Zhenfan is folded into Lelang. Four Commanderies page: 'Zhenfan was absorbed into Lelang in 82 BCE'. The Zhenfan page says its 'territorial jurisdiction is unclear', so the region is a placeholder (confidence 1). The Lelang page has Zhenfan and Lintun abolished 'after Emperor Wu's death' (Wu died 87 BCE), which disagrees.

region.text: the Lintun prefectures left after 82 BCE: 'New Dongyi prefecture is in Wonsan' and Buer at Anbyon (Lintun page); the rest of old Lintun, 'almost the same as the current Gangwon Province', went to the Ye

ledger.note: 75 BCE: what is left of Lintun passes to Lelang. Four Commanderies page (Lintun section): 'Lintun was transferred to Lelang in 75 BCE'; the Lintun page quotes Bowman that 'parts of old Lintun merged into Lelang' about then, while its own text has seven prefectures incorporated into Lelang in 82 BCE. Counterpart is Xuantu because in the Four Commanderies page's chain Lintun was merged into Xuantu in 82 BCE. The Lintun page says nine of its fifteen prefectures were abolished in 82 BCE (the Ye then 'become independent', Eastern Ye page, see dongye), so only the Wonsan-Anbyon coast is drawn as Lelang's.

region.text: Lelang, seized by Wang Tiao: 'a Chinese born in Lelang, seized power in Lelang and killed the governor'

ledger.note: 25: Wang Tiao seizes Lelang. 'In 25 CE, Wang Tiao, a Chinese born in Lelang, seized power in Lelang and killed the governor.' The page gives no extent for his hold; the core is assumed.

region.text: Lelang, retaken from Wang Tiao: 'the rebellion was stopped by Wang Zun, whom Emperor Guangwu of Han appointed as governor'

ledger.note: 30: the Han recover Lelang. 'In 30 CE, the rebellion was stopped by Wang Zun, whom Emperor Guangwu of Han appointed as governor.'

region.text: Nangnang in northwestern Korea, attacked by Goguryeo: 'He also defeated the Nakrang Kingdom in northwestern Korea in 32'

ledger.note: 32: Daemusin's war for Nangnang reaches the commandery. The Daemusin page: 'After fending off a China's attack in 28, he sent his son, Prince Hodong ... to attack the Nangnang Commandery' and 'defeated the Nakrang Kingdom in northwestern Korea in 32'. The Lelang page does not mention a Goguryeo conquest; the disagreement is noted in the notes.

region.text: Nangnang, destroyed by Goguryeo: 'He destroyed Nangnang in 37'

ledger.note: 37: Goguryeo destroys Nangnang. 'He destroyed Nangnang in 37, but an Eastern Han army sent by Emperor Guangwu of Han, captured it in 44.' The page does not say where Nangnang lay beyond 'northwestern Korea'.

region.text: Nangnang, taken by Goguryeo until the Han counter-stroke of 44

ledger.note: 37: the fighting over Nangnang ends in Goguryeo's favour until 44.

region.text: Nangnang, recaptured: 'an Eastern Han army sent by Emperor Guangwu of Han, captured it in 44'

ledger.note: 44: the Eastern Han take Nangnang back from Goguryeo (Daemusin page).

region.text: the southern half of Lelang, made into Daifang: 'Gongsun Kang created it in 204'; the Daifang page puts it 'around Hwanghae'

ledger.note: 204: Gongsun Kang cuts Daifang from Lelang's southern half. Four Commanderies page: 'Gongsun Kang created it in 204'; the Lelang page says 'sometime between 204 and 220', the Gongsun Kang page 'around this time' after 204.

204: Lelang is held by the Gongsun of Liaodong. Gongsun Kang page: 'In 204, he inherited his father's appointment and controlled the territories of Liaodong, Xuantu and Lelang commanderies' (Gongsun Du had 'taken control of the existing Daifang and Lelang commanderies' earlier, undated). The commandery stays a Han commandery in name; the metropole tint passes to the Gongsun of Liaodong (gongsun-liaodong).

238: Lelang passes to Cao Wei. 'an alliance between Wei and Goguryeo destroyed their common enemy' Gongsun Yuan in 238 and 'Wei took over all of Gongsun Yuan's territories, including Lelang and Daifang.' The Lelang page dates the Wei takeover to 236 ('In 236, under the order of Emperor Ming of Cao Wei'); the Daifang, Xuantu and Goguryeo-Wei pages say 238, which is used.

region.text: the Ye under the Marquis of Bunai, 'brought back under the influence of the commanderies of Lelang and Daifang'

ledger.note: 245: after the Wei war the Ye come under Lelang and Daifang. Goguryeo-Wei War page: 'the Ye and Okjeo tributaries' were brought 'back under the influence of the commanderies of Lelang and Daifang'; the Ye 'expected to provide provisions and transportation whenever Lelang and Daifang went off to war'. The year is the end of the war; the page gives no later date. The Ye are drawn as Goguryeo vassals by the goguryeo dossier; the two tints overlap and the renderer should let the commandery win from 245.

region.text: the Okjeo tribes defeated by Wang Qi, 'brought back under the influence of the commanderies of Lelang and Daifang'

ledger.note: 245: the (South) Okjeo tributaries pass under the commanderies. Wang Qi 'reached the Okjeo lands and defeated the South Okjeo' (3,000 killed or captured); the Cliopatria Dong-okjeo shape of 127-153 is used for the extent (its row ends 153).

265: Lelang passes to the Jin. 'As the only remaining territory in Korea, Lelang was then inherited by the Jin dynasty.' The page gives no year; 265, the start of Cliopatria's Western Jin, is a bridge (confidence 1).

region.text: the Ye, no longer tributary to Lelang when the commandery fell

ledger.note: 313: the commandery's tributaries are released with its fall. The Lelang page does not mention the Ye; the end of the tint with the commandery is a bridging judgment.

region.text: the Okjeo, no longer tributary to Lelang when the commandery fell

ledger.note: 313: as for the Ye, the tint ends with the commandery (bridging judgment).

union.text: the Lintun prefectures left after 82 BCE: 'New Dongyi prefecture is in Wonsan' and Buer at Anbyon (Lintun page); the rest of old Lintun, 'almost the same as the current Gangwon Province', went to the Ye

region.text: Lelang, 'annexed by Goguryeo under King Micheon' in 313; after 204 Lelang held Pyongyang, South Pyongan and the Wonsan coast (Hwanghae was Daifang's, lost to Goguryeo in 314)

ledger.note: 313: Goguryeo annexes Lelang. 'In 313, the territory of Lelang was annexed by Goguryeo under King Micheon.' The Four Commanderies page adds that Murong Hui 'relocated the remnants of the commandery to the west within Liaodong'. The matching entry is in the goguryeo dossier (gain 313 from lelang-commandery). region.text: Lelang, handed to Goguryeo; the commandery's remnants moved to Liaodong

ledger.note: 313: the last Chinese commandery on the peninsula ends. 'Liaodong and Lelang leaders led over a thousand households to submit to Murong Hui' and Goguryeo 'attacked and annexed the commandery in 313' (Four Commanderies page).

wars.name: Han conquest of Wiman Joseon
wars.outcome: Han victory: 'Han dynasty destroys Wiman Chosŏn in 108 BCE and establishes the Four Commanderies'.
wars.note: The page names only the year 108 BCE for the destruction; the opening year of the war is not on the pages opened (the start is set to -109 only as a bridge).

wars.name: Wang Tiao's rebellion in Lelang
wars.outcome: Rebel hold of Lelang from 25 to 30; ended by the governor Wang Zun appointed by Guangwu.

wars.name: Goguryeo-Han war over Nangnang
wars.outcome: Korean chronicle account: Goguryeo defeats Nangnang in 32, destroys it in 37; an Eastern Han army retakes it in 44.
wars.note: The Lelang page is silent on all of it.

wars.name: Goguryeo-Wei War
wars.outcome: Cao Wei victory: Hwando destroyed; after 245 the Ye and Okjeo tributaries return to the influence of Lelang and Daifang.
wars.note: Liu Mao and Gong Zun, the grand administrators of Lelang and Daifang, marched south through the Seven Counties of Lingdong; six counties submitted.

wars.name: Goguryeo annexation of Lelang
wars.outcome: Goguryeo annexes the commandery under King Micheon.

notes:
Colony dossier for the Han (then Cao Wei and Jin) commandery at Pyongyang; no Cliopatria row. Cliopatria's Han Dynasty (-91..206), Cao Cao (207..223), Cao Wei (224..264) and Western Jin (265..312) shapes all reach North Korea (bbox east edge 127E), so they already contain this land; the han-dynasty dossier (ea-02) and the others must either subtract the commandery or let this dossier's colony tint win. Cliopatria has Xin Dynasty shapes for 6..29 and no Han or Xin shape at all for 30..42, so the commandery is the only cover for its land in those years.

Disagreements between pages: (1) Lintun and Zhenfan: the Lelang page has both abolished after Emperor Wu's death and Xuantu moved; the Four Commanderies page has Zhenfan absorbed into Lelang and Lintun into Xuantu in 82 BCE and Lintun transferred to Lelang in 75 BCE; the Lintun page's own text has seven prefectures incorporated into Lelang in 82 BCE. This dossier follows the Four Commanderies chain (82 Zhenfan to Lelang; 75 old Lintun from Xuantu to Lelang). (2) Wei takeover: 236 on the Lelang page, 238 on four others (238 used). (3) The Goguryeo conquest of Nangnang (32-44) is on the Daemusin page only; the Lelang page records Wang Tiao 25-30 and nothing for 32-44; the Daemusin page's 'Nakrang Kingdom in northwestern Korea' and 'Nangnang Commandery' are not tied to the Han commandery in so many words, so the episode is confidence 2 and the contest drawing should not override the commandery's ledger.

States that need dossiers: wang-tiao (rebel, 25-30, counterpart of the 25 and 30 events), zhenfan-commandery, xuantu-commandery, daifang-commandery, gongsun-liaodong (all by this batch, jk-02-x). Gazetteer: 'Gyeonggi' stands in for Zhenfan (location unclear); no region 'Lelang' exists (the goguryeo dossier suggested one).
